title: Positron Emission Tomography/Computed Tomography with [18F]FDG in Fever, Bacteraemia and Inflammation of Unknown Origin
content: Fever of unknown origin (FUO), inflammation of unknown origin (IUO), and bacteraemia of unknown origin (BUO) are diagnostic challenges with marked aetiological heterogeneity and considerable clinical overlap. FUO and IUO share the same underlying causes and diagnostic algorithm, and [18F]FDG PET/CT is the imaging technique with the highest diagnostic yield in both, with a yield that increases when inflammatory markers are elevated at the time of the study. A negative scan, in turn, carries prognostic value, as it is associated with a higher probability of spontaneous remission. In bacteraemia, [18F]FDG PET/CT can identify the underlying cause in BUO and detect metastatic foci in complicated bacteraemia, especially in Staphylococcus aureus bacteraemia and in patients with implanted devices. This narrative review summarises the methodological aspects (patient preparation, acquisition protocol and interpretation of uptake patterns), limitations, prognostic value and position of [18F]FDG PET/CT within current diagnostic algorithms, illustrated with representative clinical cases.
